options.text: Most common paraneoplastic syndrome associated is Hypercalcemia

questions.stemHtml: A 14-year-old girl is presenting with cola coloured urine. On physical examination, her blood pressure was 154/100 mm Hg. Renal biopsy was performed and electron microscopy was showing the features shown in the below given image. Most likely diagnosis in this case will be?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) Acute proliferative glomerulonephritis

questions.stemHtml: A 45-year-old man presenting with nausea, upper abdominal pain, and jaundice following a heavy bout of drinking in a celebration party. What is the nature of the accumulations seen in the biopsy?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) Cytokeratin 8

questions.stem: A patient presented with development of seizures for which the CT guided biopsy was done. Histopathology reported the presence of psammoma bodies. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis for this patient?

questions.stemHtml: A 12-year-old boy was having abdominal pain, melena and perioral melanosis. Histopathology of the lesion is shown below in the given image. Which of the following is most likely to be associated with this condition?

questions.stem: A 9-year old child presents with hypoalbuminemia, edema, hyperlipidemia and proteinuria. The edema in the periorbital region initially and eventually spreads to the rest of the body. The patient is given steroid therapy and the disease goes away. What is a key morphological feature of the patient's disease?

options.text: Hemosiderin laden macrophages in the kidney

questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) The child with proteinuria and steroid responsive suggestive of MINIMAL CHANGE DISEASE which shows fusion of foot process.
